english: Open application preferences and saved server settings. Application preferences include command suggestion order. Select an option to edit it, then Apply or Save as appropriate.

Edit the application-wide custom key bindings. No custom bindings are installed by default. Add a key and choose an action, then Apply or Save. Escape discards changes made since opening or applying the table.
Open the separate command input. Suggestions help discover commands; selecting one inserts it for review before execution. Your conversation draft is preserved.
Keep connections running while releasing the current terminal. Resume the session with vipirc --resume. Pending setup or credential operations can require waiting before detaching.

The command screen has its own input, preserving the conversation draft. Down focuses suggestions; Up/Down selects; Enter copies the selection for editing. Up from the first suggestion returns to input. Right at the end completes a command name.
Settings offers Common, Recent history, Most used with this config, Alphabetical, and Contextual. Contextual uses the screen that opened the command prompt. Other matching commands remain available.

Delete removes a selected Recent history entry or resets a selected personal usage count in Most used. Command arguments and credentials are never saved in personal usage counts. ? explains a highlighted suggestion; in the input field it types a question mark.

The vipirc main screen provides the current server and nickname, Settings, Key bindings, Manual, Command, Background, About and the license. Up/Down selects an item; Enter opens it. / opens the command prompt with client context. B returns to the conversation. Escape opens the quit question.
The top categories lead to servers, channels, queries, activity and transfers when those categories are available. Each screen retains its own selection.

These lists show views already open in the selected server session. Up/Down selects a view; Left/Right selects Open, New, Part or Close as appropriate; Enter performs the selected action. Channel 0 is the server. /cl and /channels show local channel views; /list [MASK] [OPTIONS] opens the sortable network channel directory. /ql shows private conversations.
Channel 0 contains server replies and notices. /join and /list work here without selecting a chat conversation.
This is a private conversation. Open selects it without sending. Close discards its retained view and draft after any required confirmation.
You are joined to this channel. Part leaves it but keeps its history and unfinished draft. Close removes the view.
You are not joined to this channel. The retained view keeps its scrollback and unfinished draft. Use /join to join again, or Close to remove it.
